Main.sentence: ___E:Elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elections_in_the_United_States)___ were held in the United States on November 4, 2014, in the middle of ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ 's second term. A typical ___E:six-year itch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-year_itch)___ ___E:midterm election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_midterm_election)___ suffered by most second-term presidents, this election saw the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ expanding their majority in the ___E:House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ and winning control of the ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ , while furthering their gains in the ___E:governorships U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States))___ and ___E:state legislatures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_legislature_(United_States))___ .
Because of these Republican gains, the election was commonly cited as a ___E:"red wave" U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_elections_in_the_United_States)___ election.

Republicans won a net gain of nine Senate seats, the largest Senate gain for either party since the ___E:1980 United States elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_United_States_elections)___ .
In the House, Republicans won a net gain of thirteen seats, giving them their largest majority since the ___E:1928 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_United_States_elections)___ .
In state elections, Republicans won a net gain of two gubernatorial seats and flipped control of ten legislative chambers.
Various other state, territorial, and local elections and referendums were held throughout the year.

With total spending reaching $3.7 billion, the midterm election, at the time, was the most expensive in history, being surpassed by the ___E:2018 midterm election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_United_States_elections)___ four years later.

The 2014 election also saw the lowest ___E:turnout U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_turnout)___ since ___E:1942 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_United_States_elections)___ , with just 36.4% of eligible voters voting.

Coupled with the 2010 midterms earlier in the Obama administration, this election marked the first time since the Reagan Administration that a two-term president's party suffered net losses in both houses of Congress in both midterm elections.

Major issues of the election included income inequality,  and the ___E:Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patient_Protection_and_Affordable_Care_Act)___ (commonly referred to as "Obamacare"), which Republicans sought to repeal.
Democrats promoted their proposal to increase the ___E:minimum wage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_wage_in_the_United_States)___ .
In the lead-up to the 2014 election, Republicans harshly criticized the Obama administration for four ebola cases in the United States that were diagnosed weeks prior to the election.
The American media intensely covered the ebola scare.
However, immediately after the election, Republicans dropped Ebola as an issue.
Studies found that Republican rhetoric and media coverage of the Ebola scare helped Republican candidates in the 2014 election.

Although it generated much debate in early 2014, the ___E:Keystone Pipeline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystone_Pipeline)___ ultimately received little attention in the election, with environmentalists instead focused on fighting ___E:global warming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming)___ and supporting the ___E:EPA's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency)___ proposed regulations on ___E:greenhouse gas emissions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions)___ .
Another potentially important issue, ___E:net neutrality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_neutrality)___ , received little attention during the campaign.
National ___E:exit polling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exit_polling)___ showed that 45% of voters said the economy was their most important issue.

This was a decline from 2010 and 2008 (when 59% of voters and 63% of voters, respectively, named it as their top issue), but was still the most common issue cited by voters as most important to them.  Smaller numbers of voters named health care, foreign policy, or illegal immigration as their top issues,  or same-sex marriage, Ebola, or the ___E:legalization of marijuana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legalization_of_marijuana)___ as their top issues.
With a final total of 247 seats (56.78%) in the House and 54 seats in the Senate, the Republicans ultimately achieved their largest majority in the U.S.
Congress since the ___E:71st Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/71st_United_States_Congress)___ in 1929.
All 33 seats in ___E:Senate Class II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classes_of_United_States_Senators#Class_II)___ were up for election.
Additionally, three special elections were held to fill vacancies in Class III.

Of the 36 Senate races, the Republican Party won 24 (a net gain of nine seats,  which represents the largest gain for a party in the Senate since 1980, and the largest Senate gain in a midterm since 1958) and the Democratic Party won 12, thus resulting in the Republicans regaining control of the Senate for the first time since 2006, with a total of 54 seats.

The race in Louisiana headed to a ___E:run-off U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run-off_election)___ on December 6, 2014, in which Rep. ___E:Bill Cassidy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cassidy)___ (R) defeated 3-term incumbent Sen. ___E:Mary Landrieu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Landrieu)___ 55.9% to 44.1%.
All 435 voting seats in the ___E:United States House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ were up for election.

Elections were held to select the ___E:delegates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delegate_(United_States_Congress))___ for the ___E:District of Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia)___ and four of the five ___E:U.S. territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_insular_area)___ .

The only seat in the House not up for election was the ___E:Resident Commissioner of Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resident_Commissioner_of_Puerto_Rico)___ , who serves a four-year term. The Republican party won 247 seats (a net gain of 13 seats) and the Democratic Party, 188 seats.

Thus, the Republicans gained their largest majority in the House since 1928. [citation needed] Nationwide, Republicans won the popular vote for the House of Representatives by a margin of 5.7 percent.

On March 11, there was ___E:a special election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Florida%27s_13th_congressional_district_special_election)___ for Florida's 13th congressional district, won by the Republican Party.

Elections were held for the ___E:governorships U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor#United_States)___ of 36 U.S. states and three ___E:U.S. territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_insular_area)___ .

The Republican Party won 24 of the 36 state governorships for a net gain of two seats, as they picked up open Democratic-held seats in Arkansas, Maryland and Massachusetts and defeated incumbent governor ___E:Pat Quinn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Quinn_(politician))___ in Illinois, while Republican incumbents ___E:Tom Corbett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Corbett)___ of ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Pennsylvania_gubernatorial_election)___ and ___E:Sean Parnell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parnell)___ of ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Alaska_gubernatorial_election)___ respectively lost to Democrat ___E:Tom Wolf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Wolf)___ and independent ___E:Bill Walker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Walker_(American_politician))___ .

This cycle marked the first time an incumbent governor running for re-election in Pennsylvania lost in the modern era. The final total, as a result, was 31 Republican governors, 18 Democratic governors, and one independent governor.

In the table below, the US state governorships held by Democrats included: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Kentucky, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, and West Virginia in addition to Washington, DC and Virgin Islands.

Elections to ___E:state legislatures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_legislature)___ were held in 46 ___E:U.S. states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state)___ in 2014 with a total of 6,049 seats up for election (82 percent of the total number of state legislative seats in the United States).
Six territorial chambers were up in four territories and the ___E:District of Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ .
Prior to the general election, Republicans regained control of the ___E:Virginia Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Senate)___ after winning a decisive August special election.

They had lost control at the start of the year due to the ___E:election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Virginia_lieutenant_gubernatorial_election)___ of Democratic ___E:lieutenant governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_Virginia)___ ___E:Ralph Northam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Northam)___ .

In the general election, ___E:Republicans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ initially gained control of nine legislative chambers: both chambers of the ___E:Nevada Legislature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_Legislature)___ (which gave them a trifecta for the first time since 1931), the ___E:Minnesota House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_House_of_Representatives)___ , the ___E:New Hampshire House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_House_of_Representatives)___ , the ___E:New Mexico House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_House_of_Representatives)___ for the first time since 1955, the ___E:West Virginia House of Delegates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_House_of_Delegates)___ , the ___E:Colorado Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Senate)___ , the ___E:Maine Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Senate)___ , and the ___E:New York Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Senate)___ , which was previously under a Republican-led coalition.

This increased the total number of Republican-controlled state houses from 58 to 67. The day after the election, Republicans, who achieved a 17–17 tie in the ___E:West Virginia Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Senate)___ , gained control of that chamber as well thanks to the defection of State Senator ___E:Daniel Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Hall_(West_Virginia_politician))___ , thus increasing their total gains to ten, for a final total of 68 state houses won.  This allowed Republicans win control of either chamber of the West Virginia legislature for the first time since 1933.

Nationwide voter turnout was 36.4%, down from 40.9% in the ___E:2010 midterms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_elections)___ and the lowest since the ___E:1942 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_United_States_elections)___ , when just 33.9% of voters turned out, though that election came during the middle of ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ .

The states with the highest turnout were Maine (59.3%), Wisconsin (56.9%), Alaska (55.3%), Colorado (53%), Oregon (52.7%) Minnesota (51.3%), Iowa (50.6%), New Hampshire (48.8%), Montana (46.1%) and South Dakota (44.6%), all of which except for Iowa and Montana featured a competitive gubernatorial race and all of which except for Maine and Wisconsin also featured competitive Senate races.
The states with the highest turnout that had no Senate or gubernatorial race that year were North Dakota (44.1%) and Washington state (38.6%).

The states with the lowest turnout were Indiana (28%), Texas (28.5%), Utah (28.8%), Tennessee (29.1%), New York (29.5%), Mississippi (29.7%), Oklahoma (29.8%), New Jersey (30.4%) and West Virginia and Nevada (31.8%).
Indiana and Utah had no Senate or gubernatorial elections and the others all had races for at least one of the posts, but they were not considered competitive.
Turnout in Washington, D.C. was (30.3%).

According to CNN, Americans aged between 18 and 29 accounted for 13% of voters,  down from 19% in the ___E:presidential election two years before U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

Analysis by the ___E:Pew Research Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center)___ found that 35% of non-voters cited work or school commitments, which prevented them from voting, 34% said they were too busy, unwell, away from home or forgot to vote, 20% either didn't like the choices, didn't know enough or didn't care and 10% had recently moved, missed a registration deadline or didn't have transportation.

The New York Times counts apathy, anger and frustration at the relentlessly negative tone of the campaigns as the reasons of low turnout and stated, "Neither party gave voters an affirmative reason to show up at the polls."

___E:Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut)___ State Representative ___E:Christina Ayala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Ayala)___ (Democrat) was arrested in September 2014 on 19 voting fraud charges, specifically "eight counts of fraudulent voting, 10 counts of primary or enrollment violations and one count of tampering with or fabricating physical evidence."  In September 2015 she pleaded guilty to state election law violations, received a one-year sentence (suspended) along with two years 'conditional discharge', and agreed not to seek elective office for two years.
Her mother, Democratic Registrar of Voters Santa Ayala, was also the subject of an investigation in the case, but was not charged.

___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ State Senator ___E:Roderick Wright U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roderick_Wright_(politician))___ (Democrat) resigned from office in September 2014 and was sentenced to 90 days in ___E:Los Angeles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles)___ county jail for perjury and voter fraud.
Despite being convicted months earlier for 8 felonies, Wright was allowed to take a paid leave of absence as state senator.

In Chicago, election judges said they had received automated phone calls between October–November 3 with apparently false instructions about voting or required training, according to the Chicago Sun-Times .

In ___E:Pontiac, Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontiac,_Michigan)___ , local Democrats cited reports of voter harassment and intimidation by Republicans over questioning legally-cast ballots with election workers repeatedly having had to ask them to step aside.
A clerk called police for help.

In June 2013, the Supreme Court invalidated part of the ___E:Voting Rights Act of 1965 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voting_Rights_Act_of_1965)___ , permitting nine (mostly Southern) states to change their election laws without advance federal approval.
Since 2010, 22 states enacted new ___E:voting restrictions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voting_restrictions)___ .

The 2014 federal election was the first federal election where 15 states enacted new ___E:voting restrictions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voting_restrictions)___ , many of which faced challenges in court.
Scattered issues with voting machines occurred, with miscalibrated machines recorded a vote cast for one candidate as a vote for another candidate.
They occurred in Virginia,  Maryland,  Illinois,  and North Carolina.

In Bexar County, Texas, the Republican candidate for governor, ___E:Greg Abbott U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Abbott)___ , was accidentally replaced on the ballot by ___E:David Dewhurst U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst)___ on one machine, on which 12 votes were cast before the problem was caught.
